questions.question: An `` has a `srcset` with w descriptors but no `sizes` attribute. What happens when it is shown as a 300px thumbnail?
options: The browser measures the CSS width first and picks a small file
sizes defaults to 100vw, so the browser assumes a full-viewport-width slot and may download a much larger file than needed
The srcset is ignored and only src is used
questions.explanation: The browser chooses a candidate before layout, using sizes. Without sizes it assumes 100vw, so thumbnails over-download.

questions.question: Which is the correct treatment for the hero image that is the page's LCP element?
options: loading="lazy" so it does not block other resources
decoding="async" and no width or height
Load it eagerly with fetchpriority="high" and explicit width and height
Put it in a CSS background with no preload
questions.explanation: Lazy-loading the LCP image delays it until layout. fetchpriority="high" moves it ahead of other images, and dimensions reserve its space.

questions.question: How do the `width` and `height` attributes on an `` prevent layout shift in a responsive layout that also uses `height: auto`?
options: They fix the image at exactly those pixel dimensions on every screen
They make the image download faster
They are only used by search engines
The browser derives an aspect ratio from them before the file loads and reserves the right amount of space, while CSS still scales the image
questions.explanation: Modern browsers map width and height attributes to an internal aspect-ratio, so space is reserved up front without breaking responsive sizing.

questions.question: In a `<picture>` element with several `<source>` children, which source does the browser use?
options: The first source whose media and type both match
The smallest file among all sources
The source with the highest resolution
questions.explanation: Sources are evaluated in order and the first match wins, so list preferred formats (AVIF before WebP) and specific media conditions first.
